services.name: Blotato Engine
services.tagline: Unified social API, MCP server and full web console for 9 platforms. Self-hosted, unlimited posts, zero subscription.
services.summary: Blotato sells a unified social media API and MCP server for $29/mo. This engine reproduces the whole surface — publishing, scheduling, comments, DMs, keyword automations, analytics, visual generation and source repurposing — across 38 REST endpoints and 17 MCP tools, plus a nine-screen web console. Same request shapes, same tool names, no per-seat billing and no post caps.
highlights: 38 REST endpoints
17 MCP tools
Nine-screen web console
Nine platform connectors
Scheduling and weekly slots
Keyword DM automations
Six PNG templates
Source extraction and repurposing

services.name: Lead Engine
services.tagline: Prospect search and contact enrichment: work emails, provider-sourced personal emails and phone numbers.
services.summary: Self-hosted prospecting and enrichment workspace inspired by SalesQL. Search by role, company, industry, location and headcount; reveal work email for one credit only when found; process LinkedIn URL and CSV enrichment jobs; verify emails; organize folders; run simulated campaigns with open/click tracking; connect AI agents using MCP. Real provider-backed details require your own API keys. Without one, the system can generate a work-email candidate from a public company domain and check MX, but never invents a personal email or phone.
highlights: Prospector filters and natural-language filter parsing; searches cost 0 credits
One credit per successful email reveal; no result means no charge
Work email candidates use ranked patterns and MX checks
Direct email and phone are returned only by configured providers
LinkedIn URL and CSV enrichment jobs, folders and verifier
Campaign sequences and tracking; send simulation by default
Six MCP tools and a nine-screen UI

features.title: Prospector
features.body: Filter by title, company, industry, location, seniority and headcount. Searching never uses credits.

features.title: Contact reveal
features.body: Reveals work email confidence/status. One credit only when an email is found. Unavailable data is not fabricated.

features.title: LinkedIn URL enrichment
features.body: Parse profile URLs and enrich via configured Hunter, Apollo or PDL providers. Does not scrape LinkedIn or bypass sign-in/anti-bot controls.

features.title: Bulk CSV enrichment
features.body: Upload LinkedIn URLs, names/company, or email addresses. Poll jobs and download enriched CSV.

features.title: Email verifier
features.body: Syntax, role account, MX and optional SMTP checks. SMTP probe is off by default.

features.title: Folders and campaigns
features.body: Save contacts in lists. Build sequences and track opens/clicks. Sends are simulated unless SMTP is explicitly configured.

features.title: MCP and API
features.body: Search, reveal, enrich, verify, folders and credits via MCP/API.

services.name: Back in Stock
services.tagline: Restock waitlists that actually notify people. Self-hosted, no $19-99/mo per store.
services.summary: Back in Stock by Amp charges Shopify merchants $19 to $99 a month to collect restock waitlists and email shoppers when a sold-out variant returns. This engine reproduces the core loop: per-variant waitlist signup, a restock trigger that queues one notification per waiter, preorder capture, admin stats and per-variant CSV export, plus a storefront demo and admin console. Notifications are recorded as dry_run by default and are never labelled sent unless SMTP was actually configured.
highlights: 20/20 checks passing against a live server
Per-variant waitlists, no shopper account needed
Restock trigger queues one notification per waiter
Preorder capture on sold-out variants
Admin console and storefront demo
Per-variant CSV export
Dry-run by default, never fakes a delivery

features.title: Waitlists
features.body: Shoppers subscribe to one sold-out variant with an email. Duplicate signups are reported instead of duplicated.

features.title: Restock trigger
features.body: Setting stock from 0 to positive queues a notification row for every waiting subscriber and flips them to notified.

features.title: Preorders
features.body: Capture intent on sold-out variants with quantity, independent of the waitlist.

features.title: Admin
features.body: Stats, variant list with waiting counts, notification log, and CSV export per variant.

features.title: Honest sends
features.body: SEND_MODE=dry_run records notifications without transmitting. Nothing is reported as delivered.

prereqs: No Shopify account needed for the demo

install.desc: Create the environment and install FastAPI.

install.title: Run
install.desc: Start the storefront and admin console on port 8600.

usage.title: Join a waitlist
usage.desc: A sold-out variant accepts an email with no auth. A duplicate signup returns duplicate:true instead of creating a second row.

usage.title: Restock and notify everyone waiting

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8600/api/auth/login \

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8600/api/variants/2/stock \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"stock": 25}'

endpoints.desc: Status, send mode, variant and waiting counts

services.name: Churn Buster
services.tagline: Failed-payment recovery that cancels the dunning the moment they pay. No $269/mo floor.
services.summary: Churn Buster sells failed-payment recovery and cancellation flows starting at $269 a month, scaling with MRR. This engine reproduces the recovery loop: Stripe-shaped webhook intake, dunning campaigns with ordered steps and delays, duplicate suppression, recovery that cancels every pending email, recovery analytics with MRR at risk and recovered MRR, an admin console and a CSV report. Emails are recorded as dry_run unless SMTP is configured, and webhook signature verification activates as soon as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set.
highlights: 21/21 checks passing against a live server
Stripe-shaped webhook with optional HMAC signature check
Three-step dunning campaign with delays
Recovery cancels pending sends
Duplicate failures do not re-enrol a customer
Recovery rate, MRR at risk, recovered MRR
Dry-run by default, never fakes a delivery

features.title: Failure intake
features.body: invoice.payment_failed and charge.failed open a failure and enrol the customer. A simulator does the same without Stripe.

features.title: Campaigns
features.body: Ordered steps with per-step delays. The seeded campaign fires at 0, 1 day and 3 days.

features.title: Recovery
features.body: invoice.paid or a manual mark flips the failure to recovered and cancels every queued email for it.

features.title: Analytics
features.body: Failure counts, recovery rate, MRR at risk and recovered MRR, computed from the tables not estimated.

features.title: Honest sends
features.body: SEND_MODE=dry_run records dispatch without transmitting. Nothing is labelled sent unless SMTP was used.

prereqs: No Stripe account needed for the simulator or the test suite

usage.title: Open a failure without Stripe
usage.desc: Creates the customer if needed, opens a failure and queues one email per campaign step.
usage.code:
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8610/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@churnbuster.local","password":"churnbuster123"}' | jq -r .token)

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8610/api/simulate/payment-failure \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"customer_email":"maya@example.com","amount_cents":4900,"mrr_cents":4900}'

usage.title: Recover with a Stripe-shaped webhook
usage.desc: Payment lands, the failure closes and every pending dunning email is cancelled.

endpoints.desc: Status, send mode, open failures, queued emails

verify.code:
cd services/churn-buster
uv run python tests/test_churn_buster.py

# recorded on this machine:
# ===== 21/21 checks passed =====

notes: SEND_MODE defaults to dry_run. Dispatch records emails, it does not transmit them.
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET unset means webhooks are accepted and labelled stripe-sim. Set it in production.
This engine orchestrates communication and reporting. Charge retries belong to Stripe.
Cancellation flows, A/B tests and segmentation are not implemented yet.

faq.q: Does it retry the card charge?
faq.a: No. Stripe owns retry logic. This engine handles the customer communication and the recovery analytics around it.

faq.q: Will a real Stripe webhook work?
faq.a: Yes once STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set. The endpoint accepts the Stripe event shape and verifies the stripe-signature HMAC.

monetization.detail: The original starts at $269/mo and scales with MRR. Run one instance for your own book of business.
Host per client on your own infrastructure and bill below the incumbent's MRR-scaled tier.
Wire SMTP and a scheduler, then sell the sending layer as the paid extra.

services.name: Bannerbear Engine
services.tagline: Define a template once, render unlimited PNG variants. No $49-299/mo credit meter.
services.summary: Bannerbear sells credit-metered template image rendering from $49 to $299 a month. This engine reproduces the core: templates with named text and image layers, an async render queue that returns 202 and a job id, real PNG output at the template's dimensions, project-scoped bearer keys, and a credit ledger that refuses a render with 402 when the balance is empty. Image assets are uploaded locally, never fetched from a URL, which removes the SSRF surface.
highlights: 15 pytest checks passing
Independent render verified: PNG 1080x1350, 26089 bytes
Credit ledger debits exactly one unit per render
402 when a project runs out of credits
Project keys shown once, stored hashed
No third-party rendering key required

features.title: Templates
features.body: Named text and image layers with position, size and colour, stored as JSON and validated before use.

features.title: Async renders
features.body: POST /api/renders returns 202 plus a job id, then poll queued, rendering, done or failed.

features.title: Credits
features.body: Each accepted render reserves a credit, writes a usage row, and refunds with a compensating row if the render fails.

features.title: Project keys
features.body: Admin issues per-project bearer keys, hashed at rest and printed once.

features.title: 402 on empty
features.body: A project without credits is refused instead of being served for free.

usage.title: Render a template variant
usage.desc: Templates are defined once; a render overrides only the layers you name.
usage.code:
JOB=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8620/api/renders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"template_id":"'$TEMPLATE'","overrides":{"headline":{"text":"PROOF"}}}' | jq -r .job_id)

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -o out.png \
  http://127.0.0.1:8620/api/renders/$JOB/download

endpoints.desc: Issue a project key, shown once
Queue a render, returns 202 and a job id

verify.title: Run the suite
verify.code:

uv run --with pytest --with httpx --with pillow pytest tests/test_bannerbear.py -q

# recorded: 15 passed in 18.78s

notes: PNG only. Video, animation and AI image generation are not implemented.
Image assets are uploaded locally, never fetched from a URL, which removes the SSRF surface.

BANNERBEAR_ADMIN_PASSWORD defaults to bannerbear123 on this build. Change it before exposing the port.

faq.q: Does it need a Bannerbear account?
faq.a: No. Rendering is local Pillow output. No third-party key is involved.

faq.q: What happens when credits run out?
faq.a: The render is refused with 402 instead of being served for free.

monetization.detail: The original meters $49/$149/$299 tiers. Run one instance for unlimited internal renders.
Sell render credits to teams that want the endpoint without running Python.
Ship ready-made JSON templates for social cards, certificates and quote images.

services.name: Zigpoll Engine
services.tagline: Post-purchase surveys with a public embed separated from admin credentials. Signed webhooks included.
services.summary: Zigpoll sells post-purchase surveys and response analytics for Shopify merchants. This engine reproduces the part that actually matters: four distinct question types, survey create/update/list, anonymous public responses keyed by a public survey id that is separate from the admin credential, authenticated admin reads, aggregates computed from raw rows, CSV export, and HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks that refuse plain-HTTP destinations. A bad signature is rejected, and the test suite proves it rather than asserting it in prose.
highlights: 21/21 checks passing on both the contract port and an override port
Four distinct question types, not one generic type
Public response id separated from admin credentials
HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks, bad signature rejected
HTTPS-only webhook destinations
Aggregates verified against raw rows
No baked password: startup fails with setup instructions

features.title: Surveys
features.body: Create, update and list surveys with single choice, multi choice, rating and free-text questions.

features.title: Public responses
features.body: Anonymous responses go to a public survey id with no auth, keeping the admin credential out of the browser.

features.title: Signed webhooks
features.body: Response events are HMAC-SHA256 signed over the raw body with a per-survey secret, and plain HTTP destinations are refused.

features.title: Analytics
features.body: Per-survey aggregates and CSV export, checked against the raw response rows.

features.title: No default secret
features.body: First boot requires ZIGPOLL_ADMIN_PASSWORD and fails with instructions if absent.

install.title: Set the admin password
install.desc: Required on first start. No default ships.

usage.title: Verify signed webhooks yourself
usage.desc: A bad signature must be refused. This is the check that the paid product actually enforces.
usage.code:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8630/api/webhooks/test \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Zigpoll-Signature: sha256=deadbeef' \
  -d '{"survey_id":"demo"}'
# expect 401 or 403, never 200

verify.title: Run the suite
verify.code:
cd services/zigpoll-engine
ZIGPOLL_TEST_PORT=8631 uv run --with pytest --with httpx pytest tests/ -q

# recorded: 21 passed on 8630 and 21 passed on 8631

notes: Zigpoll tier pricing is UNVERIFIED in the research snapshot, so no price ladder is claimed here.
No Shopify order context: the public id model is implemented, the Shopify embed is not.
The webhook receiver is a test endpoint. Wire your own consumer to validate signatures in production.

faq.q: Why is the public survey id separate from the admin credential?
faq.a: Because embedding an admin key in a storefront page would leak it to every visitor. The separation is the security property.

faq.q: Does it need a Zigpoll account?

monetization.detail: Run unlimited surveys on your own infrastructure instead of a metered subscription.
Host per merchant with their own webhook secrets and CSV exports.
The Shopify order-context embed is the natural paid extension, since it is the part not implemented here.

ui.intro: Admin console at / and public embed at /s/<public_id> on port 8630.
